articles.title: Sinner splits with Darren Cahill, ropes in Stan Wawrinka's coach Magnus Norman - India Today
articles.summary: Sinner splits with Darren Cahill, ropes in Stan Wawrinka's coach Magnus Norman India Today
articles.content: Jannik Sinner will begin a new chapter in his coaching career after confirming that Darren Cahill will leave his team at the end of the 2026 season, bringing an end to a hugely successful partnership that helped the Italian establish himself among the leading players in men's tennis.Sinner has appointed former world No. 2 Magnus Norman to join his coaching team from December. The Swede will work alongside Simone Vagnozzi, who has been part of the Italian's set-up since 2022.Cahill joined Sinner's team in June 2022 and had initially planned to step away at the end of the 2025 season. However, he agreed to stay on for another year, extending a partnership that yielded five Grand Slam titles and helped Sinner reach the world No. 1 ranking.In a message shared on social media on Friday, Sinner paid tribute to the Australian, describing him as an important influence on and off the court."Darren has been an incredibly important part of my journey. I want to thank Darren for his belief in me, his honesty and his dedication. He has helped me grow both as a player and as a person, and his guidance will stay with me throughout my career," Sinner said.The Italian added that while their coaching partnership was coming to an end, their friendship would continue. He also thanked Cahill for the five seasons they had spent together, saying he would not forget a single day of their time working together.Cahill, who has coached four players to the top of the world rankings during his career, also acknowledged the relationship. He described working with Sinner as a special honour and praised the Italian's humility, dedication and trust in his team.The coaching change comes at the end of a season in which Sinner has been forced to contend with a knee injury. He has not played since beating Alexander Zverev in the Wimbledon final in July and has already announced that he will not compete in the remaining ATP tournaments this year. Alexander Zverev is set to finish 2026 as the year-end world No. 1.WHO IS MAGNUS NORMANNorman brings considerable experience as both a former player and a coach. The 50-year-old Swede reached a career-high ranking of world No. 2 in 2000 and was a French Open finalist that year, losing to Gustavo Kuerten.His biggest achievements, however, have come from the coaching box, particularly during his association with Stan Wawrinka. Norman began working with the Swiss in 2013 and helped him win three Grand Slam titles in as many consecutive years.Wawrinka claimed his maiden major at the 2014 Australian Open, defeating Rafael Nadal in the final. He followed that up with victories over Novak Djokovic in the 2015 French Open final and the 2016 US Open final. Under Norman, Wawrinka also climbed to a career-high world No. 3.Norman also coached compatriot Robin Soderling, guiding him to consecutive French Open finals in 2009 and 2010. Soderling famously became the first player to beat Rafael Nadal at Roland Garros in 2009. Norman has also worked with former Australian Open champion Thomas Johansson.Away from the tour, Norman co-founded the Good to Great Tennis Academy in Sweden with former players Mikael Tillstrom and Nicklas Kulti.For Sinner, the appointment brings in a coach with a proven record of helping elite players make the jump from the top of the rankings to Grand Slam success. Norman's task will be to build on the foundations laid by Cahill and Vagnozzi as the Italian looks to remain at the summit of men's tennis.- Ends

articles.title: Maharashtra govt accepts MBBS Interns' demand for stipend hike, monthly pay to rise from 18k to Rs 25k - Medical Dialogues
articles.summary: Maharashtra govt accepts MBBS Interns' demand for stipend hike, monthly pay to rise from 18k to Rs 25k Medical Dialogues
articles.content: Mumbai: In a latest development, the Maharashtra Government has accepted the demand for a stipend hike for MBBS intern doctors, which would increase their monthly stipend from Rs 18,000 to Rs 25,000.The decision is expected to bring relief to interns who had been holding peaceful protests against the low stipend with the support of the Association of State Medical Interns (ASMI).Medical Dialogues had earlier reported that the medicos associated with ASMI had warned of launching a statewide strike if the Government failed to provide a satisfactory response to their demands by November 1, 2026. The demands of the association are an increase in the monthly stipend from Rs 18,000 to Rs 30,000, a 3% annual increment, and fair compensation by taking into account the rising costs of food, accommodation, travel, and other essential expenses.Also read- Maharashtra MBBS interns demand Rs 30k stipend, warn of statewide strike from November 2MBBS interns in Maharashtra, who have completed their MBBS degree and are currently undergoing Compulsory Rotatory Medical Internship (CRMI) in government and affiliated medical colleges across Maharashtra, have been raising concerns over the current stipend for the past two months, citing the rising cost of living, accommodation, transportation, food, and other daily expenses.As per an Instagram post shared by the association, its representatives were called for a meeting held on November 5, 2026, at Mantralaya in Mumbai to discuss the proposed stipend revision for MBBS interns. The meeting was convened by the Maharashtra Medical Education Department in the presence of the State Medical Education Minister.Following the meeting, the Association of State Medical Interns (ASMI) informed interns that their demand for an increase in the monthly stipend had been accepted. However, the official Government Resolution (GR) is expected to take around one to one-and-a-half months to be issued due to government procedures.The association described the development as a major achievement for ASMI and the interns who had collectively raised the demand for a stipend hike. It also urged interns to continue supporting each other until the official GR is released."Guys, the meeting has successfully concluded, and our demand for a stipend hike has been accepted! The revised stipend will be ₹25,000 per month. The official GR is expected to take around 1–1.5 months due to government procedures. This is a big achievement for ASMI (Association of State Medical Interns) and every intern who stood united in this fight. Let’s continue supporting each other until the official GR is released. Together we fought, together we achieved," ASMI said in an Instagram post. Also read- Maharashtra MBBS interns demand stipend hike from Rs 18k to Rs 30k per month

articles.summary: Maharashtra grants one-year age relaxation for state recruitment exams India Today
articles.content: The Maharashtra government has granted a one-time relaxation of one year in the upper age limit for candidates appearing for state recruitment examinations, extending the concession until December 31, 2027, as per PTI.The decision, announced on Thursday, is expected to benefit candidates who became ineligible because of delays in recruitment advertisements and selection procedures.WHO WILL GET THE ONE-YEAR AGE RELAXATION?The General Administration Department announced the decision through a government resolution. It said the relaxation would apply to Maharashtra Public Service Commission recruitment advertisements published between January 1 and November 5 this year where the selection process has not begun.The concession will also apply to fresh MPSC recruitment advertisements issued between November 5 and December 31, 2027, according to PTI.The state government clarified that the one-year relaxation would also apply to examinations conducted by recruitment agencies other than the MPSC.It will cover posts where the maximum age limit under the relevant service recruitment rules differs from the limit set in the government resolution dated April 25, 2016.The latest resolution directed the MPSC to take the necessary steps to give a one-time opportunity to candidates who become eligible under the relaxation but could not submit their applications earlier.However, the concession will not apply to advertisements issued on or after January 1, 2028. The existing upper age limit under the relevant service recruitment rules or the April 25, 2016 resolution will continue to apply to such recruitment drives.WHY HAS MAHARASHTRA EXTENDED THE AGE LIMIT?The decision follows repeated protests by competitive examination aspirants in Maharashtra seeking an age-limit relaxation for recruitment to government posts.In January this year, thousands of MPSC aspirants demonstrated in Pune ahead of the Group-B non-gazetted preliminary examination. They sought a one-year relaxation in the upper age limit for Police Sub-Inspector recruitment.The protests followed delays in issuing recruitment advertisements, which candidates said had left several otherwise eligible aspirants overage. The protesters also demanded that the cut-off date for calculating age be revised to January 1, 2025.In December 2024, the state government had announced a similar one-time relaxation for MPSC recruitment after delays in the selection process linked to changes in reservation arrangements.“The concession is being considered in connection with recommendations made by a high-level committee constituted to comprehensively examine the state's existing recruitment examination system and suggest necessary reforms,” the government resolution issued on Thursday said, according to PTI.The one-year relaxation will, therefore, cover eligible recruitment advertisements issued up to December 31, 2027, while the existing age limits will again apply to advertisements issued from January 1, 2028.- EndsRead | Maharashtra MPSC panel recommends over 16,000 Group-C vacancies for 2026 examRead | Marathi now compulsory for Classes 1 to 10 in all Maharashtra schools

articles.title: Maharashtra govt approves one-year age relaxation for recruitment exams, panel proposes over 16,000 MPSC Group C vacancies - The Hindu
articles.summary: Maharashtra govt approves one-year age relaxation for recruitment exams, panel proposes over 16,000 MPSC Group C vacancies The Hindu
articles.content: Mumbai The Maharashtra government on Thursday (November 5, 2026) approved a one-time, one-year relaxation in the upper age limit for recruitment examinations, following recommendations by a high-level committee that also proposed increasing Maharashtra Public Service Commission (MPSC) Group C vacancies to over 16,000. The seven-member committee, headed by Additional Chief Secretary V. Radha, was constituted on September 4 to review the State’s recruitment examination system and recommend measures to improve transparency and prevent irregularities. It submitted its interim report to the government on Thursday (November 5, 2026). MPSC examination: Maharashtra government appoints Commission to inquire into malpractices, paper leaks MPSC examination: Maharashtra government appoints Commission to inquire into malpractices, paper leaks November 16 is the deadline for candidates, students and other stakeholders to submit their statements to the panel MPSC examination: Maharashtra government appoints Commission to inquire into malpractices, paper leaks storyline 1 According to the report, around 12 lakh candidates have applied for the MPSC Group C Combined Preliminary Examination 2026, for which more than 5,000 vacancies have been advertised. With government departments submitting requisitions for over 11,000 additional posts, the committee has recommended including these vacancies through a corrigendum. Under a Government Resolution issued on Thursday (November 5, 2026), the age relaxation will apply to recruitment advertisements issued from January 1, 2026, where no stage of the selection process has been completed, and to fresh advertisements issued until December 31, 2027. The relaxation also covers recruitment examinations conducted by agencies other than the MPSC. The commission has been directed to provide a special opportunity for newly eligible candidates to apply. The existing upper age limits will apply to advertisements issued from January 1, 2028. MPSC paper ‘leak’: Fourth Commission official arrested, total arrests rise to 13 MPSC paper ‘leak’: Fourth Commission official arrested, total arrests rise to 13 The accused, identified as Rohit Kolatakke, an assistant section officer with the MPSC, allegedly obtained the confidential question set from Abhijit Lendve, an under-secretary with the commission, who was arrested earlier in the case MPSC paper ‘leak’: Fourth Commission official arrested, total arrests rise to 13 storyline 1 Welcoming the recommendations, Nitin Andhale, an MPSC student movement organiser, said they addressed two major demands raised by aspirants during discussions with the government. “We welcome the government’s decision on the age relaxation and the move towards recruiting for 16,000 posts. It is a good beginning, but the government must also fulfil its promise to restore the objective examination pattern,” he said. Mr. Andhale criticised the descriptive pattern used for the State Services main examination, arguing that it disadvantaged candidates from rural and economically weaker backgrounds. He claimed that coaching for descriptive examinations could cost up to ₹2 lakh, forcing aspirants to relocate to cities such as Pune and Mumbai. “The descriptive pattern is for the rich, while the objective pattern is for poor students. A student from a farming family can prepare for an objective examination while staying in their village,” he said. Describing the descriptive format as a barrier to equal opportunity, he added, “The descriptive pattern is a ‘Dronacharya’ pattern that will exploit students like ‘Ekalavya’.” He also questioned the MPSC’s capacity to evaluate descriptive answer sheets, citing the rechecking of main examination papers. He alleged that the commission lacked adequate arrangements for evaluating such papers and said the government should reconsider continuing with the descriptive format. Mr. Andhale also called for the 2025 State Services examination to be brought under the scope of the separate inquiry into alleged MPSC irregularities, claiming that it had been excluded despite concerns over the examination and its evaluation process. Referring to the government’s earlier assurance to students, he warned of renewed protests if the objective examination pattern was not restored. “If the government does not implement the objective pattern as promised when we called off our agitation, lakhs of students across Maharashtra will take to the streets,” he said. Meanwhile, the committee has recommended retaining the existing examination pattern and syllabus for the Group C preliminary examination, which is separate from the State Services main examination pattern opposed by Mr. Andhale. It has also recommended announcing the main examination syllabus for newly included categories of posts at the earliest. As a precautionary measure, the committee has recommended cancelling the question-paper preparation process undertaken so far and preparing fresh papers through a secure procedure. Other proposals include stringent safeguards for printing, storing and transporting question papers and Optical Mark Recognition (OMR) answer sheets, along with police deployment, CCTV surveillance, signal jammers and trained personnel at examination centres. While the government has approved the age relaxation, the committee’s other recommendations, including the proposed increase in Group C vacancies, remain subject to further decisions.

articles.contentMarathi: Mumbai The Maharashtra government on Thursday (November 5, 2026) approved a one-time, one-year relaxation in the upper age limit for recruitment examinations, following recommendations by a high-level committee that also proposed increasing Maharashtra Public Service Commission (MPSC) Group C vacancies to over 16,000. The seven-member committee, headed by Additional Chief Secretary V. Radha, was constituted on September 4 to review the State’s recruitment examination system and recommend measures to improve transparency and prevent irregularities. It submitted its interim report to the government on Thursday (November 5, 2026). MPSC examination: Maharashtra government appoints Commission to inquire into malpractices, paper leaks MPSC examination: Maharashtra government appoints Commission to inquire into malpractices, paper leaks November 16 is the deadline for candidates, students and other stakeholders to submit their statements to the panel MPSC examination: Maharashtra government appoints Commission to inquire into malpractices, paper leaks storyline 1 According to the report, around 12 lakh candidates have applied for the MPSC Group C Combined Preliminary Examination 2026, for which more than 5,000 vacancies have been advertised. With government departments submitting requisitions for over 11,000 additional posts, the committee has recommended including these vacancies through a corrigendum. Under a Government Resolution issued on Thursday (November 5, 2026), the age relaxation will apply to recruitment advertisements issued from January 1, 2026, where no stage of the selection process has been completed, and to fresh advertisements issued until December 31, 2027. The relaxation also covers recruitment examinations conducted by agencies other than the MPSC. The commission has been directed to provide a special opportunity for newly eligible candidates to apply. The existing upper age limits will apply to advertisements issued from January 1, 2028. It is a good beginning, but the government must also fulfil its promise to restore the objective examination pattern,” he said. Mr. Andhale criticised the descriptive pattern used for the State Services main examination, arguing that it disadvantaged candidates from rural and economically weaker backgrounds. He claimed that coaching for descriptive examinations could cost up to ₹2 lakh, forcing aspirants to relocate to cities such as Pune and Mumbai. “The descriptive pattern is for the rich, while the objective pattern is for poor students. A student from a farming family can prepare for an objective examination while staying in their village,” he said. Describing the descriptive format as a barrier to equal opportunity, he added, “The descriptive pattern is a ‘Dronacharya’ pattern that will exploit students like ‘Ekalavya’.” He also questioned the MPSC’s capacity to evaluate descriptive answer sheets, citing the rechecking of main examination papers. He alleged that the commission lacked adequate arrangements for evaluating such papers and said the government should reconsider continuing with the descriptive format. Mr. Andhale also called for the 2025 State Services examination to be brought under the scope of the separate inquiry into alleged MPSC irregularities, claiming that it had been excluded despite concerns over the examination and its evaluation process. Referring to the government’s earlier assurance to students, he warned of renewed protests if the objective examination pattern was not restored. “If the government does not implement the objective pattern as promised when we called off our agitation, lakhs of students across Maharashtra will take to the streets,” he said. articles.content: राज्य सरकारने अल्पसंख्याक समाजासाठी सुरू केलेली स्वतंत्र हेल्पलाईन सुविधा बंद५ फेब्रुवारी २००९ रोजी शासन निर्णयाद्वारे हेल्पलाईनची निर्मिती करण्यात आली.स्वतंत्र हेल्पलाईनऐवजी आता शासनाच्या ११२ हेल्पलाईनचा वापर करण्याचे निर्देश देण्यात आले.राज्यात दुष्काळाचं संकट आलं असून या दुष्काळात शेतकऱ्यांच्या मदतीसाठी सरकारकडून उपाययोजना केली जातेय. दुसरीकडे सरकारी तिजोरीवर भार वाटणाऱ्या योजना सुद्धा गुंडाळण्यात येत आहेत. त्याचदरम्यान राज्य सरकारनं एक महत्त्वकांक्षी योजना बंद करण्याचा निर्णय घेतलाय. अल्पसंख्याक समाजातील नागरिकांच्या अडीअडचणी आणि तक्रारींचे निवारण करण्यासाठी सुरू केलेली स्वतंत्र हेल्पलाईन सुविधा बंद करण्याचा निर्णय घेतला आहे. या हेल्पलाईनऐवजी नागरिकांनी आता शासनाच्या '११२' या हेल्पलाईनचा वापर करावा, असे निर्देश देण्यात आले आहेत. यासंदर्भात राज्य सरकारने शासनादेश जारी केलाय. .राज्य सरकारकडून कर्मचाऱ्यांना दिवाळी भेट; १० सणांच्या अग्रिम रकमेत मोठी वाढ .अल्पसंख्याक समाजातील नागरिकांना विविध प्रश्न आणि अडचणी उद्भवल्यास त्यांचे वेळीच निराकरण व्हावे, त्यांच्या शंकांचे निरसन व्हावे आणि योग्य मार्गदर्शन मिळावे, या उद्देशाने राज्य सरकारने ५ फेब्रुवारी २००९ रोजीच्या शासन निर्णयानुसार स्वतंत्र हेल्पलाईन सुविधा निर्माण केली होती. महाराष्ट्र राज्य अल्पसंख्याक आयोगाच्या कार्यालयात १ सप्टेंबर २०१० पासून ही सुविधा प्रत्यक्ष सुरू करण्यात आली. सन २००९-१० पासून अल्पसंख्याक विभागामार्फत ही योजना राबवली जात होती..राजू शेट्टींना अटक होण्याची शक्यता; एकीकडे चर्चा सुरू असतानाच आंदोलनस्थळी पोलीस फौजफाटा वाढवला .मात्र, आता या योजनेचा आढावा घेऊन ती बंद करण्याचा निर्णय घेण्यात आलाय. नियोजन विभागाच्या उपसचिवांच्या अध्यक्षतेखाली १० ऑगस्ट २०२६ रोजी झालेल्या बैठकीत या हेल्पलाईनच्या फलनिष्पत्तीचा आढावा घेण्यात आला. त्यानंतर स्वतंत्र हेल्पलाईनऐवजी शासनाच्या '११२' या हेल्पलाईनचा वापर करण्याचे निर्देश देण्यात आले..दरम्यान, राज्य सरकारने यापूर्वीच योजनांच्या खर्चाचा आढावा घेण्याचे निर्देश दिले होते. वित्त विभागाच्या पत्रानुसार, मागील तीन आर्थिक वर्षांत ज्या राज्य योजनांवर प्रत्यक्ष खर्च २५ कोटी रुपयांपेक्षा कमी झालाय, अशा योजनांचा आढावा घेऊन त्या बंद करता येतील. इतर योजनांमध्ये एकत्रित करता येतील का, याची तपासणी करण्यास सांगण्यात आले होते.सकाळ+चे सदस्य व्हाशॉपिंगसाठी 'सकाळ प्राईम डील्स'च्या भन्नाट ऑफर्स पाहण्यासाठी क्लिक करा.Read Marathi news and watch Live TV. एकीकडे चर्चा सुरू असतानाच आंदोलनस्थळी पोलीस फौजफाटा वाढवला .मात्र, आता या योजनेचा आढावा घेऊन ती बंद करण्याचा निर्णय घेण्यात आलाय. नियोजन विभागाच्या उपसचिवांच्या अध्यक्षतेखाली १० ऑगस्ट २०२६ रोजी झालेल्या बैठकीत या हेल्पलाईनच्या फलनिष्पत्तीचा आढावा घेण्यात आला. त्यानंतर स्वतंत्र हेल्पलाईनऐवजी शासनाच्या '११२' या हेल्पलाईनचा वापर करण्याचे निर्देश देण्यात आले..दरम्यान, राज्य सरकारने यापूर्वीच योजनांच्या खर्चाचा आढावा घेण्याचे निर्देश दिले होते. वित्त विभागाच्या पत्रानुसार, मागील तीन आर्थिक वर्षांत ज्या राज्य योजनांवर प्रत्यक्ष खर्च २५ कोटी रुपयांपेक्षा कमी झालाय, अशा योजनांचा आढावा घेऊन त्या बंद करता येतील. इतर योजनांमध्ये एकत्रित करता येतील का, याची तपासणी करण्यास सांगण्यात आले होते.सकाळ+चे सदस्य व्हाशॉपिंगसाठी 'सकाळ प्राईम डील्स'च्या भन्नाट ऑफर्स पाहण्यासाठी क्लिक करा.Read Marathi news and watch Live TV.
